name: Neutral monism
plain_explanation: If mind and matter are not two different kinds of stuff, but experience shows up sometimes as a 'knower' and sometimes as a 'known,' then the world's basic material is neither mental nor physical -- it is 'neutral,' prior to that distinction.
precise_definition: The doctrine, advocated by James's followers though not developed by James himself, that the material of which the world is constructed is neither mind nor matter but something anterior to both, following from radical empiricism's abolition of the subject-object dualism as a distinction of 'stuff.'
why_it_mattered: It offers a way to dissolve the traditional mind-matter problem at its root, rather than solving it within the old dualist framework.
historical_origin: Drawn as an implication of James's 1904 essay by those who agreed with him, though James himself did not draw it out.
associated_philosopher: William James (doctrine developed by his followers)
competing_positions: James's own apparent, if unintended, drift toward Berkeleian idealism
influence_on_later_thinkers: Russell connects it directly to the mind-matter theory he develops in the closing chapter on logical analysis, where physics and psychology are said to be converging on treating both mind and matter as 'convenient ways of grouping events.'
